drivingQuestion: Why did the Sages fix the mention of rain, the request for rain, and havdala each in the particular blessing the mishna names?
outcomeNote: Each of the mishna's three placements is given a reason; Rav Aḥa Karḥina'a's objection to the 'between two letters' derivation is answered and confirmed by Ulla.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַזְכִּירִין גְּבוּרוֹת גְּשָׁמִים: מַאי טַעְמָא?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» We learned in the mishna that «one mentions the might of the rains» in the second blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of the revival of the dead. The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» that the might of the rains is mentioned specifically in that blessing?

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁשְּׁקוּלָה כִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים לְפִיכָךְ קְבָעוּהָ בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said: Because» the might of the rains «is equivalent to the resurrection of the dead,» as rain revives new life in the plant world (Jerusalem Talmud), «therefore it was inserted in» the blessing of «the revival of the dead. »

«And» we also learned in the mishna that the «request» for rain is added to «the blessing of the years.» Here, too, the Gemara asks: «What is the reason» that the request for rain is recited specifically in that blessing?

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא פַּרְנָסָה, לְפִיכָךְ קְבָעוּהָ בְּבִרְכַּת פַּרְנָסָה.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said: Because» rain is a component of «sustenance, therefore it was inserted in the blessing of sustenance» as part of our request for bountiful sustenance.

We also learned in the mishna that «havdala,» distinguishing between Shabbat and the weekdays, is added «in» the blessing of: «Who graciously grants knowledge.» Here too the Gemara asks: «What is the reason» that havdala is recited specifically in that blessing?

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא חָכְמָה, קְבָעוּהָ בְּבִרְכַּת חָכְמָה. וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהִיא חוֹל, לְפִיכָךְ קְבָעוּהָ בְּבִרְכַּת חוֹל.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said:» Havdala is recited in that blessing «because it» requires «wisdom» to distinguish between two entities, «they established it in the blessing of wisdom. The Rabbis say» a different reason: «Because» havdala «is» the distinction between the sacred and the «profane,» the Sages «established it in the blessing of weekdays.» The first three blessings of the Amida prayer are recited both on weekdays and on Shabbat and Festivals. The blessing: Who graciously grants knowledge, is the first of the blessings recited exclusively during the week.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: גְּדוֹלָה דֵּעָה, שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בִּתְחִלַּת בְּרָכָה שֶׁל חוֹל.
segments.en: Having mentioned the blessing of wisdom, the Gemara cites that which «Rav Ami said» with regard to knowledge: «Great is knowledge that was placed at the beginning of the weekday blessings;» an indication of its significance.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: גְּדוֹלָה דֵּעָה, שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי אֵל דֵּעוֹת ה׳״. וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דֵּעָה — אָסוּר לְרַחֵם עָלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי לֹא עַם בִּינוֹת הוּא עַל כֵּן לֹא יְרַחֲמֶנּוּ עוֹשֵׂהוּ״.
segments.en: «And Rav Ami said» in praise of knowledge: «Great is knowledge that was placed between two letters,» two names of God, «as it is stated: “For God of knowledge is the Lord”» (I Samuel 2:3). «And» since knowledge is regarded so highly, «anyone without knowledge, it is forbidden to have compassion upon him, as it is stated: “For they are a people of no wisdom, so their Creator will have no compassion upon them» and their Creator will not be gracious unto them” (Isaiah 27:11). If God shows no mercy for those who lack wisdom, all the more so should people refrain from doing so.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גָּדוֹל מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנִּתַּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פָּעַלְתָּ ה׳ מִקְּדָשׁ ה׳״.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rabbi Elazar said: Great is the Holy Temple, as» it too «was placed between two letters,» two names of God, «as it is stated:» “The place in which to dwell which «You have made, Lord, the Temple, Lord,» which Your hands have prepared” (Exodus 15:17).

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דֵּעָה כְּאִילּוּ נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו. דֵּעָה נִתְּנָה בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, מִקְדָּשׁ נִתַּן בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת.
segments.en: Noting the parallel between these two ideas, «Rabbi Elazar» added «and said: Anyone with knowledge,» it is «as if the Holy Temple was built in his days; knowledge was placed between two letters» and «the Temple was placed between two letters,» signifying that they stand together.

segments.he: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא קַרְחִינָאָה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, גְּדוֹלָה נְקָמָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בֵּין שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״אֵל נְקָמוֹת ה׳״!
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa Karḥina’a strongly objects to this» approach that being placed between two names of God accords significance: «However, if so,» the same should hold true for vengeance. «Great» is «revenge that was placed between two letters, as it is stated: “God of vengeance, Lord,» God of vengeance shine forth” (Psalms 94:1).

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, בְּמִילְּתַהּ מִיהָא גְּדוֹלָה הִיא. וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא שְׁתֵּי נְקָמוֹת הַלָּלוּ לָמָּה? אַחַת לְטוֹבָה, וְאַחַת לְרָעָה. לְטוֹבָה — דִּכְתִיב: ״הוֹפִיעַ מֵהַר פָּארָן״. לְרָעָה — דִּכְתִיב: ״אֵל נְקָמוֹת ה׳ אֵל נְקָמוֹת הוֹפִיעַ״.
segments.en: «He said to him: Yes. At least in its place,» in the appropriate context, «it is great.» At times it is necessary. «That is that which Ulla said: Why» are «these two vengeances» mentioned in a single verse? «One for good and one for evil.» Vengeance «for good, as it is written: “He shined forth from Mount Paran”» (Deuteronomy 33:2) with regard to God’s vengeance against the wicked; vengeance «for evil, as it is written: “God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance shine forth”» with regard to the punishment of Israel.

moves.summary: why is rain's might mentioned in the blessing of the revival of the dead?

moves.summary: because rain is equivalent to the revival of the dead
moves.about: rain was fixed in the blessing of the revival of the dead because it is equivalent to the revival of the dead

moves.summary: the second lemma is quoted and its reason asked
moves.about: why the request for rain was fixed specifically in the blessing of the years

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: מתוך שהיא פרנסה
moves.summary: because rain is sustenance, fixed in the blessing of sustenance
moves.about: rain is sustenance, so its request was fixed in the blessing of sustenance

moves.summary: the third lemma is quoted and its reason asked
moves.about: why havdala was fixed specifically in the blessing of knowledge

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: מתוך שהיא חכמה
moves.summary: because havdala is an act of discernment, fixed in the blessing of wisdom
moves.about: havdala is an act of discernment, hence fixed in the blessing of wisdom

moves.summary: the Rabbis give a rival reason: it is the first weekday blessing
moves.about: why havdala was fixed in the blessing of knowledge — because it is an act of wisdom (Rav Yosef) or because it is the first weekday blessing (the Rabbis)

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אמי: גדולה דעה, שניתנה בתחלת ברכה של חול
moves.summary: Rav Ami praises knowledge from its placement first among the weekday blessings
moves.about: the placement of the blessing of knowledge first among the weekday blessings shows knowledge's greatness

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב אמי: גדולה דעה, שניתנה בין שתי אותיות
moves.summary: knowledge is set between two divine names, and one lacking it may not be pitied
moves.about: the verse in which knowledge stands between two divine names

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: גדול מקדש שניתן בין שתי אותיות
moves.summary: the Temple too is set between two divine names
moves.about: the verse in which the Temple stands between two divine names

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי אלעזר: כל אדם שיש בו דעה
moves.summary: the two parallels are joined: one with knowledge is as if the Temple were built in his days
moves.about: from the parallel placement of knowledge and of the Temple between two divine names, one with knowledge is as though the Temple were built in his days

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רב אחא קרחינאה: אלא מעתה
moves.summary: vengeance is also set between two divine names — is it great too?
moves.about: whether placement between two divine names really marks greatness, since vengeance is also so placed

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אין, במילתה מיהא גדולה היא
moves.summary: yes — vengeance is great in its proper place
moves.about: vengeance too is indeed great in its own place, so the objection does not overturn the rule

moves.summary: Ulla's two-vengeances exposition confirms that vengeance can be for good
moves.about: Ulla's exposition of the two vengeances, adduced to confirm that vengeance can be a good
